cells.reason: Morgan Stanley reports its fee-based/advisory revenue on client assets as Asset management revenues, which are related to advisory services associated with fee-based client assets, along with fee-based client assets and average fee rates.

items.text: Morgan Stanley defines asset management revenues in the Wealth Management segment as fees related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, and distribution of products, generally based on the net asset value of the account.
items.quote: Within the Wealth Management business segment, Asset management revenues are related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, as well as distribution of products. These revenues are generally based on the net asset value of the account in which a client is invested.
items.definition: Asset management revenues are related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, as well as distribution of products, generally based on the net asset value of the account.

items.text: Morgan Stanley defines fee-based client assets as the amount of assets in client accounts where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets.
items.quote: Fee-based client assets represent the amount of assets in client accounts where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets.
items.definition: Fee-based client assets represent the amount of assets in client accounts where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets.

items.text: Morgan Stanley reported Wealth Management asset management revenues of $18,627 million in 2025, up 13% from the prior year, reflecting higher fee-based assets due to higher market levels and cumulative positive fee-based flows.
items.quote: Asset management revenues of $18,627 million in 2025 increased 13% compared with the prior year, primarily reflecting higher fee-based assets due to higher market levels and the cumulative impact of positive fee-based flows.
